extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers in AI method development (postdoctoral researchers and junior/qualification professorship holders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting draft and full proposals to the DFG Emmy Noether Programme call for 'Methods in Artificial Intelligence', including eligibility, proposal format, selection procedure, deadlines, and institutional requirements. Targeted at prospective group leaders seeking six-year funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant status eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals can be submitted by postdoctoral researchers and holders of temporary junior or equivalent qualification professorships (W1/W2) at an early stage of their academic career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Junior professors who have successfully passed their interim evaluation and holders of comparable qualification professorships are no longer eligible. The interim evaluation must not coincide with the DFG’s proposal review process; if it does the applicant is ineligible and the proposal will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time since doctorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals can generally be submitted two to four years after completing a doctorate; applicants who have completed their doctorates within the past two years are particularly encouraged to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard DFG rules on calculating time limits apply (e.g., childcare periods are taken into account). See the Guidelines Emmy Noether Programme (DFG form 50.02) for details on time-limit calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required academic qualification level
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are expected to have obtained an above average doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of the quality of the doctorate in the application materials (see CV/publication list guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of significant preliminary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide evidence of significant preliminary work in the form of significant publications in internationally respected publication outlets or appropriate relevant experience based on industrial research in one of the aforementioned areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the draft stage include an academic CV with a list of up to ten of the most important publications. Emphasise publications or industrial outputs that demonstrate the feasibility and track record for the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: International research experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should demonstrate international research experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include research visits abroad, international research collaborations, or work experience in an international working environment. The DFG particularly encourages applicants involved in international research systems who intend to switch or return to the German system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical scope: AI methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is available for projects that involve the development or further advancement of AI methods, including theoretical foundations, analysis and evaluation. The term 'AI methods' is broadly understood and encompasses (but is not limited to) machine learning, optimisation, logic and reasoning, algorithmics, data analytics and data mining, knowledge representation, knowledge-based systems, mathematical and formal foundations, statistical learning methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly situate work within the methods-focused remit; interdisciplinary applications are acceptable provided the core is AI method development, advancement, analysis or evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project type and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should involve the development or further advancement of AI methods, or their analysis and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise methodological novelty, theoretical foundations, rigorous analysis, or thorough evaluation plans rather than only domain applications without methodological contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection procedure structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection consists of two stages; both stages use the standard criteria applicable to the Emmy Noether Programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First stage: review based on draft proposals (≤5 pages). Candidates who pass are invited to submit full proposals aligned with programme standard requirements. Second stage: review and funding decision are based on the full proposal and an oral presentation by the candidate. See Guidelines for Reviews in the Emmy Noether Programme (DFG form 10.210).

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft proposal length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft proposal must not exceed five pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some sections/subsections in the Project Description (DFG form 53.05) are omitted for the draft and should not be addressed—consult the Supplementary Explanation of Draft Proposals for Emmy Noether Groups under the AI Initiative. Include an academic CV (DFG form 53.200) as an appendix with a list of up to ten most important publications. No further attachments are required at the draft stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and forms to follow
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must follow DFG proposal preparation instructions and specific Emmy Noether Programme forms (e.g., DFG form 54.01, 50.02, 53.05, 53.200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed forms for structure and content; omitted sections for the draft are documented in the supplementary explanation. Failure to follow forms/structure may cause review-stage issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission is exclusively via the elan portal for secure data processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not already registered as an applicant with the DFG, complete registration at least one week prior to submission. For this call, register by no later than 4 June 2025 to submit the draft by 11 June 2025. You will generally receive confirmation of registration by the following working day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and timeline expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Key dates for this call: draft proposal due 11 June 2025; invitations to submit full proposals issued in early October 2025; envisaged full-proposal submission deadline 17 December 2025; DFG Joint Committee funding decisions expected 26 March 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any changes to the timeline will be announced on the DFG AI funding initiative website. Plan travel/availability for oral presentation dates and coordinate institutional approvals in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, diversity and encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: The DFG explicitly welcomes proposals from researchers of all genders and sexual identities, from different ethnic, cultural, religious, ideological and social backgrounds, from different types of institutions, and from researchers with disabilities or chronic illnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DFG encourages female researchers in particular to submit proposals. Consider indicating any diversity-relevant information in the application where appropriate (while respecting privacy and data-protection rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional good-research-practice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: DFG funding may only be awarded to institutions that have implemented the Code of Conduct – Guidelines for Safeguarding Good Research Practice as part of their internal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legally binding implementation is the responsibility of the institution's leadership. Applicants should check internally at an early stage whether their institution has implemented the Code to prevent delays in funding disbursement. See the Research Integrity portal and contact DFG’s Research Integrity team for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft-stage attachment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: At the draft stage, the only required appendix is an academic CV with up to ten publications; no further attachments are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include additional attachments for the draft unless explicitly requested. Follow the Supplementary Explanation of Draft Proposals for what to include/omit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and enquiry procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial enquiries should be sent exclusively via e-mail to ai-initiative@dfg.de; programme contacts and responsible staff are listed for specific questions (programme content, eligibility/procedural issues, administration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the specified contact route helps ensure swift processing; telephone numbers for named contacts are provided for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement for return/switch to German research system
rubrics_metrics.description: The DFG particularly encourages proposals from researchers in international research systems who would like to switch or return to the German system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relocation costs to Germany can be reimbursed; group leaders receive social-security benefits and family support. Mention plans for relocation or integration where relevant to the proposal and CV.
